goldenPoints: ASHA serves about 1,000 population in rural areas; ANM sits at the sub-centre
IMR denominator is live births; MMR is per 1,00,000 live births
PPV rises and falls with prevalence — the most-tested screening fact
Case-control gives odds ratio and suits rare diseases; cohort gives incidence and relative risk
Mode is the most frequent value; the mean is the measure wrecked by one wrong entry
Shakir tape red zone (MUAC below 11.5 cm) means severe acute malnutrition
Yellow bag: soiled and anatomical waste and expired drugs; white puncture-proof container: sharps
fIPV fractional doses are given at 6 and 14 weeks under the NIS
Tobacco-control legislation is primordial prevention; screening is secondary prevention
Quarantine began as 40 days of isolation for plague ships
intro: Community Medicine carries 30 of the 300 FMGE questions, and it is the most formula-driven subject in the paper: rates with exact denominators, colour bags, population norms, schedule ages, programme names. Almost every stem in these notes was asked in the last five years — learn the numbers here and this subject becomes free marks.

subject: Community Medicine
tagline: PSM in FMGE is denominators, colour bags, population norms and programme names — the most formula-driven 30 marks in the paper.

topics.oneLiner: Incubation period is infection-to-symptoms in one person; serial interval is onset-to-onset between linked cases.
points: Natural history of disease runs: prepathogenesis (agent–host–environment interaction) then pathogenesis
Incubation period: entry of the agent to the first symptom
Serial interval: time between onset of the primary case and onset of the secondary case it infects
Latent period: infection to becoming infectious (used for non-communicable disease as exposure-to-detection)
Quarantine originated as 40 days of isolation for ships suspected of carrying plague
Iceberg phenomenon: diagnosed cases are the tip; hidden and subclinical cases form the submerged part
Single-exposure point-source epidemic: one peak, all cases within roughly one incubation period
Propagated epidemic: person-to-person spread with successive peaks (e.g. hepatitis A in a hostel)
topics.title: Epidemiology Basics & Natural History of Disease
topics.trap: Serial interval is between onsets of two cases — not between infection and symptoms.

topics.askedAs: which design for the given scenario
topics.oneLiner: Start with disease and look back: case-control. Start with exposure and follow forward: cohort.
points: Case-control study: starts from cases and controls, looks back at exposure; yields the odds ratio
Case-control is the design for rare diseases and for outbreaks needing a quick answer (thalidomide–phocomelia was shown this way)
Cohort study: starts from exposed and unexposed, follows forward; yields incidence and relative risk
Cross-sectional (prevalence) study: exposure and disease measured at one point in time — a snapshot
Randomised controlled trial: randomisation is the main tool that removes selection bias
Phase III trial compares the new drug with standard treatment; marketing approval follows phase III
Ecological study uses group-level data and suffers the ecological fallacy
Recall bias is the classic weakness of case-control studies; attrition weakens cohorts
topics.title: Study Designs
topics.trap: A study that collects exposure history from mothers of affected and unaffected babies is case-control, even if the records are old.

topics.oneLiner: Sensitivity finds the diseased; specificity clears the healthy; PPV obeys prevalence.
points: Sensitivity = true positives ÷ all actually diseased × 100 — the test's ability to catch disease
Specificity = true negatives ÷ all actually healthy × 100 — the ability to clear the healthy
Positive predictive value rises as disease prevalence rises; it falls sharply for rare diseases
A highly sensitive test is best for screening (few cases missed); a specific test confirms
Screening is secondary prevention — presumptive identification of unrecognised disease
Wilson and Jungner criteria govern whether a disease is fit for screening
Lead-time bias makes survival look longer merely because diagnosis happened earlier
A good screening test must be acceptable, repeatable, valid and cheap
topics.title: Screening & Evaluation of Diagnostic Tests
topics.trap: For a rare disease, even a good test gives a low PPV — prevalence, not sensitivity, is the biggest influence.

topics.oneLiner: Births and deaths per 1,000 mid-year population; maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births.
points: Crude birth rate = live births in a year ÷ mid-year population × 1,000
General fertility rate = live births per 1,000 women aged 15–49 years
Total fertility rate: average children a woman would bear through her reproductive life
Infant mortality rate denominator is live births (deaths under 1 year per 1,000 live births)
Early neonatal deaths occur in the first 7 days; late neonatal deaths from day 8 to 28
Maternal mortality ratio = maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births in the same period
Deaths from accidents (e.g. electrocution) are excluded when calculating the MMR
Mid-year population (1 July) is the denominator for crude birth and death rates
Case fatality rate = deaths from a disease ÷ cases of that disease × 100
topics.title: Rates, Ratios & Vital Statistics
topics.trap: Stillbirths never enter the MMR or IMR denominator — only live births do.

topics.oneLiner: Mean chases outliers, median resists them, mode is simply the most repeated value.
points: Mode is the most frequently occurring value in a dataset
Median is the middle value; it is the best central measure for skewed data
A single wrongly recorded value (39 entered as 93) disturbs the mean the most
Normal distribution: mean ± 1 SD covers about 68%, ± 2 SD about 95%, ± 3 SD about 99.7% of values
In a normal curve, mean = median = mode
Blood cholesterol in mg/dL is measured on a ratio scale (true zero exists)
Histogram displays continuous data; bar charts compare discrete categories; scatter shows correlation
Chi-square test compares proportions in qualitative data
Standard deviation measures dispersion around the mean
topics.title: Biostatistics Essentials
topics.trap: Mode is not the largest value and not the average — it is the most common value.

topics.oneLiner: Birth rate stays high in stages 1–2 while the death rate falls — that gap is the population explosion.
points: Demographic cycle stage 1 (high stationary): high birth rate and high death rate
Stage 2 (early expanding): death rate falls, birth rate stays high — fastest population growth
Stage 3 (late expanding): birth rate starts falling; India is in this stage
Stage 5 (declining): birth rate falls below death rate, population shrinks
Sex ratio above 1,000 means more females than males in the population
An eligible couple is a married couple with the wife aged 15–49; registers are kept at the sub-centre
Couple protection rate is the percentage of eligible couples effectively protected by contraception
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015
The Census (Registrar General of India) is the main source of complete demographic data
topics.title: Demography & Family Planning Indicators
topics.trap: The highest growth is in stage 2, not stage 1 — in stage 1 the high death rate cancels the high birth rate.

topics.oneLiner: Legislation before risk factors appear is primordial; finding disease early is secondary.
points: Primordial prevention: preventing risk factors from emerging — e.g. tobacco-control legislation
Primary prevention: health promotion and specific protection (immunisation, hand washing, ORS education)
Secondary prevention: early diagnosis and prompt treatment — all screening programmes
Tertiary prevention: disability limitation and rehabilitation
Sub-centre covers 5,000 population in plains (3,000 in hills); PHC 30,000 (20,000 hills)
CHC covers 1,20,000 in plains (80,000 in hills) and is the first referral unit level with specialists
One ASHA serves about 1,000 rural population; she is a link worker, not a salaried employee
Ayushman Bharat: PM-JAY gives ₹5 lakh cover per family per year for hospitalisation
Referral chain: sub-centre → PHC → CHC → district hospital
topics.title: Levels of Prevention & the Health Care System
topics.trap: Government tobacco regulation is keyed as primordial prevention, not primary — a repeated FMGE distinction.

topics.oneLiner: Birth: BCG, OPV-0, hepatitis B. 9 months: MR. 10 years: Td.
points: At birth: BCG, OPV zero dose and hepatitis B birth dose (within 24 hours)
6, 10 and 14 weeks: pentavalent, OPV, rotavirus; fractional IPV (fIPV) at 6 and 14 weeks
9–12 months: MR first dose, JE in endemic districts, PCV booster
16–24 months: MR second dose, DPT and OPV boosters
5–6 years: DPT booster; 10 and 16 years: Td
A 10-year-old attending for immunisation receives Td
BCG is a live vaccine; live vaccines are avoided in the severely immunocompromised
Vaccine vial monitor (VVM) reaching discard point means the vaccine must not be used
Shake test detects freeze damage in adsorbed vaccines like pentavalent and hepatitis B
topics.title: Universal Immunisation Programme (NIS)
topics.trap: fIPV under the current schedule is at 6 and 14 weeks — not three full IPV doses.

topics.askedAs: programme for the given condition or age
topics.oneLiner: Match the programme to its initials and age band: RBSK 0–18, NSSK newborns, Axshya TB.
points: RBSK screens children 0–18 years for the 4 Ds: defects, diseases, deficiencies, developmental delays
Navjaat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK) trains staff in essential newborn care and resuscitation
Axshya project is associated with tuberculosis control (community engagement under NTEP)
Anaemia Mukt Bharat follows a 6×6×6 strategy (6 groups, 6 interventions, 6 institutional mechanisms)
Suraksha clinics provide syndromic management of STIs/RTIs under NACP
VHND (Village Health and Nutrition Day) is held once a month at the anganwadi
National Deworming Day is observed on 10 February (with a second round on 10 August)
ICDS delivers supplementary nutrition and preschool education through anganwadi centres
IDSP runs outbreak surveillance; data flows weekly from reporting units
topics.title: National Health Programmes
topics.trap: RBSK covers 0–18 years including out-of-school children — do not limit it to school-going children.

topics.askedAs: bag colour for the given item
topics.oneLiner: Yellow burns soiled waste and expired drugs; sharps never go in a bag — they go in the white puncture-proof container.
points: Yellow bag: human anatomical waste, soiled waste, expired medicines and cytotoxic drugs (labelled)
Red bag: contaminated recyclable plastics — tubing, catheters, gloves, IV sets
White translucent puncture-proof container: sharps — needles, blades, broken glass with sharp edges
Blue bag/box: glassware (vials, ampoules) and metallic body implants
Used cotton swabs and dressings go into the yellow bag
Needle-stick injury: wash with soap and water, report, and start HIV PEP ideally within 2 hours (up to 72 hours)
Window period of HIV: the antibody test may be negative early; nucleic acid testing detects infection earliest
Anatomical and soiled waste in yellow bags is treated by incineration or deep burial
topics.title: Biomedical Waste Management
topics.trap: Cytotoxic drugs go in yellow (with a cytotoxic label), not in a separate black bag — the black bag is gone from the current rules.

topics.oneLiner: Height-for-age tells the past (stunting), weight-for-height tells the present (wasting), MUAC below 11.5 cm is SAM.
points: Shakir's tape measures mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) to screen malnutrition
MUAC below 11.5 cm (red zone) indicates severe acute malnutrition (SAM)
Chronic malnutrition is best measured by stunting — low height-for-age
Acute malnutrition shows as wasting — low weight-for-height
A child with MUAC 10.5 cm who eats the appetite test well is SAM without complications — treat in the community
Epidemic dropsy is caused by argemone oil adulteration of mustard oil
Lathyrism (spastic paralysis) follows excess kesari dal (BOAA toxin)
Endemic fluorosis comes from excess fluoride in drinking water, not from adulteration
Global Hunger Index uses undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality
topics.title: Nutrition & Nutritional Assessment
topics.trap: MUAC is age-independent between 6 and 59 months — that is exactly why Shakir's tape works in the field.

topics.oneLiner: 0.5 mg/L free residual chlorine after one hour of contact is the disinfection benchmark.
points: Free residual chlorine of 0.5 mg/L after 1 hour of contact indicates adequate water disinfection
Horrock's apparatus estimates the chlorine demand of water
Slow sand filtration purifies water largely by its biological layer (schmutzdecke)
Trickling filter / percolating methods purify sewage by aerobic bacterial action through media beds
Overcrowding criterion: more than 2 persons per room is overcrowding (sex separation adds stricter rules)
Recommended classroom space is about 10 sq ft per student
Hygrometer (psychrometer) measures humidity and dew point of air
Controlled tipping (trench method) needs roughly 1 acre of land per 10,000 population per year
Cholera and typhoid are the classic water-borne diseases used to judge a water supply
topics.title: Environment, Water & Sanitation
topics.trap: A trench-method land question is a favourite arithmetic stem — remember 1 acre per 10,000 population.

topics.oneLiner: ESI sickness benefit pays 70% of wages; silicosis is the pneumoconiosis that leads every list.
points: ESI Act: sickness benefit is 70% of wages for up to 91 days (about 3 months) in a year
ESI maternity benefit is payable for 26 weeks under the amended provisions
Silicosis (silica dust, mining and stone work) is the commonest pneumoconiosis
Byssinosis strikes cotton workers — chest tightness worst on Mondays
Bagassosis comes from mouldy sugarcane fibre (thermophilic actinomycetes)
Sickness absenteeism rate is used as an indicator of workers' health status
Ergonomics is the science of fitting the job to the worker
Lead is the classic industrial poison: anaemia, blue gum line, wrist drop
The ESI scheme covers medical benefit, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits
topics.title: Occupational Health & ESI
topics.trap: The 70%-for-3-months fact belongs to ESI sickness benefit — stems disguise it as maternity or disablement benefit.

topics.askedAs: method size, agency and target facts
topics.oneLiner: Focus group 6–12 people; WHO Geneva, 7 April 1948; SDG aims for global MMR below 70 by 2030.
points: Focus group discussion works best with 6–12 participants plus a facilitator
Role play (sociodrama) suits demonstrating skills like ORS preparation or wound care to a group
Propaganda gives one-sided facts to push a decision; health education gives facts and lets people decide
Demonstration is the most effective single method for teaching a practical skill to a rural group
ABC analysis classifies inventory by cost: A items are few but consume most of the budget
WHO headquarters is in Geneva; the WHO constitution came into force on 7 April 1948 (World Health Day)
SDG target 3.1: reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to below 70 per 1,00,000 live births by 2030
Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep are rabies-free areas of India
Disaster management cycle order: response → recovery → mitigation → preparedness (a repeating cycle)
topics.title: Health Communication, Management & International Health
topics.trap: Health propaganda and health education are opposites in these stems — propaganda conceals and compels, education informs and frees.
